cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's just been talking about Moses, Israel's leader, who put a veil over his face (2 Corinthians 3:13). Now Paul says God in His mercy has given him and the people with him this ministry.

cards.question: Since God gave them this ministry in His mercy, what does Paul say they don't do?

cards.text: Instead, Paul says they've renounced secret and shameful ways. So no sneaking, friend, and that includes the cookie hidden behind my oven timer that I know NOTHING about.

cards.question: Paul says they don't practice deceit. True or false: he says they bend the word of God a little to win people over.
Paul says they commend themselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God by ___ proclamation of the truth.

cards.text: There's that veil again. Paul says if their gospel is veiled, it's veiled to those who are perishing.
Then Paul says the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers.

cards.question: Paul says the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers. What can't they see?

cards.text: It's the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
Then Paul makes it clear they don't proclaim themselves. That one stings, friend, because I tell every baker who walks in here about this mustache. TWICE.

cards.question: Paul doesn't proclaim himself. So who does he proclaim?
Paul says he and the people with him are the Corinthians' ___ for Jesus' sake.

cards.text: Paul says God, who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness,' made His light shine in their hearts. Friend, after YEARS in a junk drawer, light in the dark hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Paul says God made His light shine in their hearts. True or false: he says that light gives them the knowledge of the glory of God in Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Now Paul paints a picture. They have this treasure in jars of clay, which is like keeping your whole paycheck in an old cookie box held shut with a rubber band.

cards.question: Why does Paul say they have this treasure in jars of clay?

answers.text: To show the power is from God
To pass it on to others

cards.text: So what's life like for a jar of clay? Paul says they're hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed, and perplexed, but not in despair.

cards.question: Paul keeps pairing a hard thing with 'but not.' What is he saying about life as a jar of clay?

answers.text: Trouble hits them but cannot break them
Trouble only comes to those who doubt
Trouble shows that God has left them

cards.text: Then Paul adds another hard thing: they're persecuted.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that when they're persecuted, they're forsaken.

cards.text: Paul says they're struck down, but not destroyed. Then he goes deeper: they always carry around in their body the death of Jesus.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says they carry the death of Jesus around so the life of Jesus may be revealed in their body.

cards.text: He says it another way: they're always consigned to death for Jesus' sake, so the life of Jesus may be revealed in their mortal body.

cards.question: So Paul sums it up: death is at work in them, but ___ is at work in the Corinthians.

cards.text: Then Paul quotes Psalm 116:10: 'I believed, therefore I have spoken.' He says they have that same spirit of faith, so they also believe and therefore speak.

cards.question: True or false: Paul knows the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise them with Jesus.
Paul looks ahead to being presented in God's presence. Who does he say will be presented there along with him and the people with him?

cards.text: Paul tells the Corinthians all this is for their benefit. God's grace keeps extending to more and more people.

cards.question: Paul says the grace reaching more and more people may cause ___ to overflow, to the glory of God.

cards.text: That line again: 'Therefore we do not lose heart.' Paul says their outer self is wasting away, and I feel that, friend, because my edges once got so soft my cookies came out looking like weather maps.

cards.question: Paul says their outer self is wasting away. True or false: he says their inner self is being renewed day by day.

cards.text: Then Paul calls their troubles 'light and momentary affliction.'

cards.question: What does Paul say this light and momentary affliction is producing for them?

cards.text: So Paul tells them where they fix their eyes: not on what is seen, but on what is unseen.

cards.question: Why do Paul and the people with him fix their eyes on what is unseen?

answers.text: Because what is unseen is eternal
Because what is seen is too painful
Because what is seen will fool them
